question: What will Turkey's month-on-month CPI inflation rate be for September 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: TCMB Market Participants Survey (Sep 7-9) expects 2.12% m/m for September; Web TÜFE nowcast 2.22%. Most of the September fuel hikes came after the survey (diesel +18.9%, gasoline +8.15% Sep 1-22, Brent >$100), and school-year price rises add pressure. Part of the education increase was front-loaded into August (+8.62% m/m). Recent Septembers: 3.23% (2025), 2.97% (2024), 4.75% (2023), but disinflation has lowered the level. Median set a bit above consensus at ~2.35. No human prediction market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers): none found.
calls.dossier:
- TCMB Market Participants Survey, Sep 2026 (fieldwork Sep 7-9, 67 respondents): expected September m/m CPI 2.12% (previous survey 2.08%); year-end 2026 CPI expectation 29.61% (previous 29.43%) [uzmanpara/forbes.com.tr, Sep 11 2026].
- Web TÜFE (independent nowcast) September m/m projection: 2.22% [turkiyegazetesi, Sep 22 2026].
- Istanbul European-side fuel, Sep 1-22 2026: gasoline +8.15%, diesel +18.9%; Brent above $100/bbl [turkiyegazetesi, Sep 22 2026]. Most of this came after the survey fieldwork.
- August 2026: gasoline +10.7%, diesel +14.4%; an economist estimated the direct CPI effect at 0.33pp. The August print was 1.84% m/m vs 1.86-1.93% consensus (AA survey range 1.25-2.10) [politikam, Sep 1 2026; tradingeconomics].
- Fuel's direct contribution to Jan-Aug 2026 CPI: 1.25pp; diesel +67% year to date [economist Yılmaz via news, Sep 2026].
- Education services rose 8.62% m/m in August 2026 (53.44% y/y), so part of the school-year increase was front-loaded before September [news, Sep 2026].
- 2026 m/m prints: Jan 4.84, Feb 2.96, Mar 1.94, Apr 4.18, May 1.71, Jun 0.99, Jul 1.78, Aug 1.84. Annual rate 31.51% in August.
- Recent September prints: 2025 3.23%, 2024 2.97%, 2023 4.75% (higher-inflation regimes; September is seasonally high because of education and clothing).
- İş Bankası expects September m/m to be above August, driven by services and food; fuel flagged as an upside risk (question background).
- TCMB policy rate held at 37%. Real-sector 12-month PPI expectation fell 0.2pp to 31% [uzmanpara, Sep 21 2026].
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the TCMB Consumer Prices table, 09-2026 row, m/m column (first TurkStat release). TurkStat release expected Mon Oct 5 2026 10:00 per Uzmanpara.
- Event window: September 2026 price month (Sep 1 -> Sep 30); as of Sep 22, about 73% elapsed.
- Searched without finding: a post-Sep-15 economist consensus update, any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market (none found), and TCMB's own monthly price-developments note for September.
calls.reference_class: September m/m CPI prints in Turkey vs the prior-month TCMB survey consensus, 2023-2025, adjusted to the 2026 disinflation regime (May-Aug 2026 avg ~1.6%)

calls.reasoning: TCMB Market Participants Survey (7-9 Sep) expected Sept m/m CPI 2.12%, before most of September's fuel hikes (diesel +18.9%, gasoline +8.15% Sep 1-22 in Istanbul as eşel mobil is phased out). WebTÜFE nowcast through Sep 22 is 2.22%, but it overshot August (2.04 vs official 1.84). Seasonal: September usually exceeds August due to education/back-to-school (2024: 2.47->2.97; 2025: 2.04->3.23). Food and a TurkStat downside-surprise tendency (Aug 1.84 vs 1.93 consensus) are the offsets. Median ~2.35. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found for Turkish CPI.

calls.reasoning: Anchors: TCMB Market Participants Survey (7-9 Sep) expects 2.12% m/m for September; the Web TUFE online nowcast shows 2.22% as of 22 Sep, but it overshot August by ~0.2pp (2.04 vs official 1.84). Upside: diesel rose ~19% and gasoline ~8% (Istanbul, 1-22 Sep) with Brent >$100; much of that came after the survey (big diesel hikes ~15-17 Sep), the fuel-price stabiliser (eşel mobil) is being phased out, and September education/clothing seasonality means Sept exceeded Aug and consensus in 2024 (2.97) and 2025 (3.23). Downside: disinflation trend, August came in below consensus, nowcast core/services moderate (1.5-1.9%). Median ~2.36, skewed up. No human market found (checked Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold: none for Turkey CPI).
calls.dossier:
- Resolution instrument: resolves off TurkStat Sept 2026 CPI m/m % (first release), mirrored in the TCMB Consumer Prices table row 09-2026; not Web TUFE, not ITO. TurkStat release: Mon 5 Oct 2026 10:00 (Uzmanpara, 21 Sep 2026).
- Event window: September 2026 price month (1 Sep -> 30 Sep); as of 22 Sep 23:30 UTC ~73% of the price month has elapsed; the value is fixed but unpublished.
- 2026 m/m prints: Jan 4.84, Feb 2.96, Mar 1.94, Apr 4.18, May 1.71, Jun 0.99, Jul 1.78, Aug 1.84 (Aug consensus was 1.93); y/y Aug 31.51% (TradingEconomics).
- TCMB Market Participants Survey, Sept 2026 (fielded 7-9 Sep, 67 respondents): September m/m CPI expectation 2.12% (up from 2.08% in the August survey); October 1.97%; year-end 29.61% (Uzmanpara/TCMB PKA).
- Web TUFE (independent online-price index), as of 22 Sep 2026: September m/m 2.22%; its August figure was 2.04% vs the official 1.84%. SA sub-indices: food 2.2, services 1.6, core measures 1.5-2.1 (webtufe.com).
- Fuel: Istanbul European side 1->22 Sep: gasoline +8.15%, diesel +18.9%; diesel ~96.3 TL/l and gasoline ~80.4 TL/l on 22 Sep; large diesel hikes around 12, 15 and 17 Sep (+7.72, +6.62, +~4.7 TL); Brent ~$104 on 17 Sep (Dunya, Bigpara, Turkiye gazetesi, 17-22 Sep 2026).
- Economist Prof. H.H. Yilmaz (1-2 Sep 2026): the phased exit from the fuel-price stabiliser (eşel mobil) plus education-season prices could push September above plan; he estimated ~1.86% m/m before the mid-month fuel hikes (politikam, ankahaber).
- Is Bankasi preview: September m/m to rise vs August on services and food; fuel is an upside risk (question background).
- Seasonality: Sept vs Aug official prints: 2024 Aug 2.47 -> Sept 2.97; 2025 Aug 2.04 -> Sept 3.23 (Sept 2025 was well above consensus). Past consensus-vs-actual monthly misses are typically 0.2-0.8pp in both directions (Jul 2025 came in below consensus, Aug 2026 slightly below).
- Real sector survey (21 Sep): 12-month PPI expectation down 0.2pp to 31%.
- Status quo: monthly prints ~1.8-2.2 in recent months, with September seasonally higher.
- Searched, absent: a Reuters/AA economist poll for Sept 2026 (none found yet; the AA poll usually comes out ~1 Oct); ITO Istanbul Sept index (not yet out); any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market on Turkish CPI (none found).
calls.reference_class: Turkish monthly CPI prints relative to TCMB survey consensus, and September prints relative to August in 2023-2025

calls.reasoning: TCMB survey (7-9 Sep) expected 2.12% before most of September's fuel hikes (diesel +18.9%, gasoline +8.15% Sep 1-22; August's smaller-but-similar hikes were worth ~0.33pp direct). Web TÜFE nowcast 2.22% but overshot August by ~0.2pp. September seasonality (education/clothing) lifted Sept over Aug by 0.5-1.2pp in 2024-25; Aug 1.84 + ~0.5 ≈ 2.35. Offsets: education partly front-loaded into August, TurkStat printed below consensus in August. Median ~2.36, mild upside skew. No human market found by any run (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers).
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agreed on every factual input (survey 2.12, Web TÜFE 2.22 with its August overshoot of ~0.2, fuel moves, release date Oct 5, no market) and on the median (~2.35). No factual dispute remained. On judgment I agree with their median: the post-survey fuel pass-through (~+0.1-0.2pp) roughly cancels Web TÜFE's upward bias and August's front-loaded education fees, and the survey plus fuel, the nowcast minus its bias, and the seasonal step from August all point to ~2.3-2.4. I widened the tails slightly, especially the upside, because single-month consensus misses of 0.5-0.8pp are common and Sept 2025 beat consensus by a lot. Reference class and dispersion basis carried forward from the runs with a small widening. No web retrieval this run.
